title: Accounting Records
text: “Well, I think the Filolial-samas have managed to change to some extent.”
Sakura-chan, Yuki-chan, Kou, and Luna-chan. With four Filolial-samas like that, they can carry even the heaviest loads with ease.
“Yeah… That’s why I’m chirping away with Keel-kun. It’s fun when I do that.”
“Oh, I see. Good luck.”
As my Father said that, Luna gave Keel a gentle, tight hug. It seems Luna really likes Keel.
“It’s super soft and feels great, but… it’s hot…”
Keel is panting with his tongue hanging out, just like a dog. I can’t understand why he’d dislike the warmth of Filolial-sama.
“Don’t hug him for too long, okay? Just like Sakura-chan, everyone has such high body temperatures that neither I nor Keel-kun can sleep soundly.”
“Okay… Then once Keel-kun falls asleep, Luna will let him wrap her up.”
“‘Let him wrap her up’? What are you planning to do?!”
Luna-chan glowed and gradually shrank, landing right in Keel’s hand. She looks just like one of Filolial-sama’s chicks.
“Piyo.”
“Ah… uh, okay. I get it. Then we can sleep together, right?”
“Piyo piyo.”
“Luna-chan? Why aren’t you talking?”
Luna-chan is chirping “piyo piyo” on top of Keel’s hand.
“Keel, she can’t talk in this form, you know?”
Sakura-chan answered Keel’s question.
“You can’t talk in this form?”
“Huh… is that so?”
“That’s right. Naofumi, didn’t you know?”
“But you guys don’t transform into such tiny forms, do you?”
“Hmm? You’re right.”
Sakura-chan tilted her head before answering. It’s such a peaceful scene. And so, the night wore on.

And so, my father had Filolial-sama and the others pull a wagon loaded with food from the Bio Plant as he made his way through Melromarc. Along the way, he treated an elderly woman suffering from an illness while posing as a medicine peddler, and in this way, he’s been working extensively to resolve the food shortages for people throughout Melromarc.

For the village in the southwest, where the problem remained unsolved even after several round trips, he left seeds as a gift. Since his level has risen considerably, he hasn’t been hunting in the Siltvelt area anymore. Well, since my father has now mastered the Portal skill, there’s really no need for me to deliver him there anymore.

However, according to my father, it would be better for him to continue peddling, so he’s decided to focus on that. But, as expected of my father, he spends his free time studying Magic and learning the Magic Letters.
By now, he’s even mastered Fast-Class Magic. This was about a week and a bit after the wave had ended.
And now, we’re inside a moving carriage.
“Hmm…”
Father is groaning as he stares intently at his ledger.
“What’s the matter?”
“Ah, well. It’s about my recent sales from peddling…”

My father shows me something. Is this… the sales report for that day? Yesterday’s sales were strong, but the day before yesterday were just so-so. Of course, both days met the target my father had set.
“What does this mean?”
“Well, this is the total sales when Keel and Elena take turns as salespeople. Or rather, when they’re in charge? Since one of them is assisting the other, after all.”
“I see… So the one with the lower sales is the Lazy Pig, then.”
When I said that, Father scratched his cheek with a troubled look.
“I’m afraid… it’s actually the opposite. Revenue is actually higher when Elena is the salesperson.”
What?! What on earth does that Lazy Pig have that contributes to sales? Doesn’t she just sleep all the time? It’s actually rare to see her not lying down.
“What do you mean by that?”
“Hmm… This might have something to do with the situation in the country of Melromarc. After all, Keel-kun is a Demi-Human, so people who discriminate against him might not buy from him…”
I see. It’s like they think, “Who knows what would happen if you ate medicine or food touched by a tainted Demi-Human?” That’s exactly the kind of thing people in this country would come up with.
“I can’t think of any other explanation.”
“I suppose so… but Elena-san hides her usual lack of motivation when serving customers and talks with a professional smile, so she comes across as friendly.”
Since she’s been deceiving me all along, I can’t say I’m surprised. But… hmm, I still find it hard to accept.
“Oink…”
The Lazy Pig is still sleeping as usual. Why is that, you ask?

“She’s good at maneuvering around customers’ haggling, and she knows just when to raise the price and sell it to them. Keel-kun’s regulars end up buying from him no matter what, but when it comes to one-time deals, Elena’s the better salesperson.”
Hmm… I thought she’d be shown the door right away, but it seems the Lazy Pig is actually somewhat useful after all. She’d better do her best to serve my Father.
“Well, lately Luna-chan has been charming everyone as Keel-kun’s partner, so his popularity has been growing, too.”
It looks like Keel is riding on Luna-chan’s back, chatting away in her carriage—a different one from the one we’re riding in. It’s a heartwarming sight.
“Naofumi, where are we going next?”
“Once we’re done loading up on food at Elena’s estate, let’s head to the eastern part of the country.”
“Got it!”

And so, the carriage continued on its way. Lately, thanks to Yuki, Kou, and Luna joining us, we’ve been able to carry much larger quantities. It actually takes quite a few days just to sell off all the food we’ve loaded onto the carriage.

It seems they’ve started selling in the Lazy Pig’s territory as well, and business is quite brisk. It appears that food distributed by the Holy Bird Sage was a line the Lazy Pig wouldn’t cross, so Father and I worked together to persuade the Lazy Pig’s mother.
“Come to think of it…”
I seem to recall Filo-tan mentioning that Father was involved in some other sales activities, but I just can’t remember what they were.
“What’s the matter?”
When the offer came up to pick up a merchant on the way, it seems the Lazy Pig had turned it down. …What was it again? Father also turned it down after just a brief conversation with that person.
“I seem to recall hearing that my future Father was selling other things as well.”
“Huh… I wonder what it was?”
“Oink…”
“Cooking… He’s not a professional chef, so he wouldn’t go that far, would he?”
The excited voices of Keel and the others are getting closer.
“Big bro! When are you gonna make us some crepes?!”
My Father looked away from the Lazy Pig. I found myself thinking it wasn’t entirely impossible. But I, Motoyasu, am convinced that even if my Father were to sell food, it would sell.
“Hmm… I wonder. Based on what Motoyasu-kun said, I can’t really picture anything else coming to mind…”
“That’s true.”

To be honest, back in the future, I was just following Father’s orders, so I don’t really know either. However, if I recall the equipment in the corner of his room from when I visited him, there might be something we can figure out from that.
“Elena, is there anything… that might give me a flash of inspiration if I were to go peddling with one Filolial and one slave each?”
“Oink…”
The Lazy Pig grunted as it swayed in the hammock.
“Huh? So that person I tried to get into a carriage with the other day is a merchant famous for jewelry?”
“Oink.”
“If that’s the case… did he teach you something?”
“Oink.”
“He’s a miser, so it’s hard to win his favor, right? But my future self managed to make a successful business just by being in this country… so maybe it’s not impossible.”

Hmm, come to think of it, there was a fancy hairpin among the things Filo-tan treasured. Did Father make that himself? Now that I think about it, I seem to recall that Keel was also wearing some kind of bone accessory around his waist.
“I wonder how they make accessories? I get the equipment part, but mines and stuff…”
“Why don’t you just ask when you go to Siltvelt?”
“But then I’d end up possessing an accessory of unknown origin, wouldn’t I?”
It’s a tricky balance. I’ll just have to be patient until the next wave, but it’s frustrating.
“Boo?”
“Should I try talking to Elena’s mom? Yeah, that might be a good idea.”
“It’s settled, then.”
“That said, she’s pretty busy with all sorts of things, so don’t get your hopes up. Actually, I feel like this kind of thing—where good taste really matters—is more up Motoyasu’s alley.”
“Hahaha, if it’s a matter of Father’s life, Motoyasu will give it his all!”
“That might be a good idea… Motoyasu, when you’re riding in the carriage, you just seem to be killing time playing around with Yuki-chan and the others.”
Father was looking at me with half-closed eyes. That’s quite unfair. If it’s Father’s command, I’ll do anything.
“Well then, I’ll ask Motoyasu to make clothes and accessories.”
“Got it!”
And so, I ended up making accessories as my task while riding in the carriage.

Oh, right—with this many people traveling together, bandits sometimes attack, but Yuki and the others took them down before Father even had a chance to step in. So even when we’re told there are bandits, my Father just casts Shooting Star Shield and doesn’t come out.
Bandits are a resource, after all. I’m the one who collects them. I release them afterward, though. They’ve been keeping a low profile lately.
Some bandits disguised as members of the Three Heroes Church also showed up when trade resumed, but I took care of them immediately.
